akhfash:5-5.t: He said ﴿فَوَصَطْنَ بِهِ﴾, and some read ﴿فَوَسَطْنَ﴾***. «[Translator's note: so in the source; the first form is spelled with ṣād, and the reading contrasted with it is presumably the doubled «فَوَسَّطْنَ».]»

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿وَالْعَادِيَاتِ﴾: the horses that run on raids and pant ﴿ضَبْحًا﴾: it is the sound of their insides when they run,

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿فَالْمُورِيَاتِ﴾: the horses that strike fire ﴿قَدْحًا﴾ with their hooves when they travel by night over stony ground,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿فَالْمُغِيرَاتِ صُبْحًا﴾: the horses that raid the enemy at the time of morning, through the raiding of their riders,

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿فَأَثَرْنَ﴾: stirred up ﴿بِهِ﴾ — in the place of their running, or at that time — ﴿نَقْعًا﴾: dust, by the vigour of their movement,

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ﴾ — with the dust — ﴿جَمْعًا﴾ of the enemy, that is, came into its midst. The verb is conjoined to the noun because [the noun] is to be interpreted as a verb, that is: "by those [fem.] that ran, then struck fire, then raided."

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ﴾, the disbeliever, ﴿لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ﴾: ungrateful, denying His blessing, Exalted is He,

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ﴾, that is, his ingratitude, ﴿لَشَهِيدٌ﴾: he bears witness against himself through what he does,

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لِحُبِّ الْخَيْرِ﴾, that is, wealth, ﴿لَشَدِيدٌ﴾, that is, intense in love of it, so he is miserly with it.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿أَفَلَا يَعْلَمُ إِذَا بُعْثِرَ﴾: is stirred up and brought out ﴿مَا فِي الْقُبُورِ﴾ of the dead, that is, they are resurrected,

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَحُصِّلَ﴾: is made clear and set apart ﴿مَا فِي الصُّدُورِ﴾: the hearts, of disbelief and faith,

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّهُمْ بِهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَخَبِيرٌ﴾: knowing, so He will recompense them for their disbelief. The pronoun refers back in the plural in view of the meaning of «الإنسان». This clause indicates the object of «يعلم», that is: "that We will recompense him at the time mentioned." «خبير» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يومئذ», while He, Exalted is He, is always aware, because it is the Day of recompense.

daas-irab:1-1.t:
﴿وَالْعادِياتِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb of swearing; ﴿ضَبْحاً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb.
The verbal clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿فَالْمُغِيراتِ﴾: conjoined to العاديات; ﴿صُبْحاً﴾: an adverb of time.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿فَأَثَرْنَ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, the nūn being its fāʿil (agent); ﴿بِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿نَقْعاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:5-5.t: Conjoined to what precedes it, and its i'rab is like it.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿لِرَبِّهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them; ﴿لَكَنُودٌ﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and ﴿كنود﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of inna; the nominal clause is the answer to an oath and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿عَلى ذلِكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them; ﴿لَشَهِيدٌ﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and ﴿شهيد﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿لِحُبِّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) شديد; ﴿الْخَيْرِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿لَشَدِيدٌ﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and ﴿شديد﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿أَفَلا﴾: the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), the fāʾ is a conjunction conjoining to an omitted, implied [clause], and لا is negative; ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position; ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿بُعْثِرَ﴾: a passive past verb; ﴿ما﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿فِي الْقُبُورِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:10-10.t:
﴿وَحُصِّلَ ما﴾: a passive past verb, and ما is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿فِي الصُّدُورِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.
The clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّهُمْ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿بِهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) خبير; ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb annexed to one like it; ﴿لَخَبِيرٌ﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and ﴿خبير﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

dervis-irab:1-11.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْعادِياتِ) The horses that run swiftly on a raid; the yāʾ is from a wāw because of the kasra before it.
(ضَبْحاً) It is the sound of their chests. In al-Mukhtār: "Ḍabaḥat al-khayl, of the pattern qaṭaʿa; al-ḍabḥ is the sound of their breaths when they run." In al-Qāmūs: "Ḍabaḥat al-khayl ḍabḥan and ḍabāḥan: they made a sound audible from their mouths that is neither neighing nor snorting; or they ran at less than a trot." Al-Farrāʾ said: "Al-ḍabḥ is the sound of horses when they run. Ibn ʿAbbās said: no animal makes the ḍabḥ except the horse, the dog and the fox. It was also said that they were muzzled so as not to neigh and let the enemy know of them, so in that state they breathed forcefully; these animals make the ḍabḥ only when their state changes from fright or fatigue." In al-Qāmūs: "Kaʿamtu l-baʿīr, like manaʿa, so it is makʿūm and kaʿīm: I tied its mouth shut so that it would not bite or eat; and what it is muzzled with is called kiʿām, like kitāb." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He swears by the horses of the raiders, which run and pant. Al-ḍabḥ is the sound of their breaths when they run. It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he imitated it, saying: 'aḥ, aḥ.' ʿAntara said:
والخيل تكدح حين تضب ... ح في حياض الموت ضبحا
(And the horses strain hard when they pant, in the pools of death, panting.)"
Al-kadḥ is earnest effort in running; ʿAntara compared death to a torrent by way of implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya), and "pools" is its imaginative embellishment (takhyīl).
(فَالْمُورِياتِ) The horses that strike fire with their hooves, i.e., strike sparks, as the fire-stick strikes fire; this is the fire of al-Ḥubāḥib. The maṣdar is awrā yūrī īrāʾan, so it is mūrin. Al-Nābigha said:
تقد السلوقي المضاعف نسجه ... وتوقد بالصفاح نار الحباحب
(She cuts through the Salūqī mail of doubled weave, and strikes with the flat stones the fire of al-Ḥubāḥib.)
Al-Ḥubāḥib, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, is the name of a miserly man who would light only a weak fire for fear of guests; so they made him a proverb, until they said "the fire of al-Ḥubāḥib" for what horses strike out with their hooves.
In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Warā l-zand yarī, of the pattern waʿada, and in one dialect wariya yariy, with kasra on both; and awrā, with alif, which is when it brings out its fire." In al-Mukhtār: "And someone else awrāhu." It is learned from what is in al-Miṣbāḥ and al-Mukhtār that it is used as a triliteral intransitive and as a quadriliteral both intransitive and transitive; and what is in the verse is of the transitive quadriliteral type.
(قَدْحاً) A maṣdar of qadaḥa; one says qadaḥtu l-ḥajar bi-l-ḥajar, i.e., I struck one against the other. The original sense of al-qadḥ is extraction, hence qadaḥtu l-ʿayn when you drain the bad water out of it; iqtadaḥtu l-zand; iqtadaḥtu l-maraq, I ladled it out. Al-miqdaḥa, with kasra on the mīm, is what fire is struck with; al-qaddāḥa and al-qaddāḥ are the stone that gives fire.
(فَالْمُغِيراتِ) The horses that raid the enemy. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Aghāra l-faras ighāratan, the noun being al-ghāra, like aṭāʿa iṭāʿatan, the noun being al-ṭāʿa: when it hastens in running; and aghāra l-qawm ighāratan: they hastened in marching." In al-Qāmūs: "Aghāra ʿalā l-qawm ghāratan and ighāratan: he drove the horses at them; aghāra l-faras: its running grew intense, in a raid or otherwise." He said:
أغار على العدو بكل طرف ... وسلهبة تجول بلا حزام
(He raided the enemy with every noble steed and tall mare that roams without a girth.)
(فَأَثَرْنَ) They stirred up. One says thāra yathūru thawran, thawarānan and thuʾūran: it was stirred; hence thārat al-fitna baynahum, strife broke out among them; thāra l-ghubār or the smoke: it rose; thāra l-jarād: the locusts appeared; thārat nafsuhu: he retched; thāra ilayhi and bihi: he leapt upon him.
(نَقْعاً) Dust. Al-naqʿ is also that a person quenches his thirst by drinking water; one says naqaʿtu ghullī bi-sharba mā'. Bashshār said:
كأن مثار النقع فوق رؤوسنا ... وأسيافنا ليل تهاوى كواكبه
(As if the rising dust above our heads, with our swords, were a night whose stars come tumbling down.)
(فَوَسَطْنَ) They came into the middle. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "One says wasaṭtu l-qawm and the place, asiṭu wasṭan, of the pattern waʿada, when you came into the middle of it; the agent is wāsiṭ, and from it the famous town in Iraq was named, because it lies in the middle of the region." In al-Mukhtār: you say jalastu wasṭa l-qawm with sukūn, because it is an adverb, and jalastu wasaṭa l-dār with vowelled middle, because it is a noun for what is surrounded by other things on its sides; every place where "between" is suitable is wasṭ with sukūn, and where "between" is not suitable it is wasaṭ with vowel, though sometimes it is given sukūn, which is not the preferred form.
The wording of al-Qāmūs: "Wasaṭahum, like waʿada, wasṭan and wasṭatan: he sat among them, like tawassaṭahum; he is wasīṭ among them, i.e., the best of them in lineage and the highest in station; the wasīṭ between disputants; and, like ṣabūr, a verse of poetry, or the smallest of them; the she-camel that fills the vessel; those that carry on their heads and backs, which are not hobbled or tethered; the one that is milked forty days after the year; Wasṭān, a town of the Kurds; Wasaṭ with vowels, a mountain and a circular tract; Wāsiṭ, a place; and wasaṭ with vowels: what lies between its two ends, like awsaṭ; and when given sukūn it is an adverb; or both apply to what is solid like a ring, whereas if its parts are distinct then it is with sukūn only; or every place where 'between' is suitable is with sukūn, and otherwise it is with vowels."
(لَكَنُودٌ) Al-kanūd: the ungrateful. Kanada l-niʿma kunūdan; from it Kinda was named, because he was ungrateful to his father and left him. From al-Kalbī: al-kanūd in the language of Kinda is the disobedient, in the language of Banū Mālik the miserly, and in the language of Muḍar and Rabīʿa the ungrateful. In al-Mukhtār: "Kanada: he was ungrateful for a favour; its pattern is dakhala; so he is kanūd, and a woman is also kanūd." Abū Umāma al-Bāhilī reported: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Al-kanūd is the one who eats alone, withholds his rifd (his giving), and beats his slave." The wording of Ibn Khālawayh: Al-kanūd is the ungrateful. Al-Ḥasan said on His saying, the Mighty and Exalted, (إن الإنسان لربه لكنود): "He recalls misfortunes and forgets favours." Al-Namir ibn Tawlab said:
كنود لا تمنّ ولا تغادي ... إذا علقت حبائلها برهن
لها ما تشتهي عسل مصفّى ... إذا شاءت وحوّارى بسمن
(Ungrateful, she neither bestows favour nor goes out in the morning, when her ties are fastened to a pledge; she has what she desires, refined honey whenever she wishes, and white flour with ghee.) [Translator's note: the rendering of the first verse is tentative.]
(بُعْثِرَ) Its explanation has often been given before. Al-baʿthara and al-baḥthara with ḥāʾ mean extracting a thing and uncovering it.

* I'rab:
(وَالْعادِياتِ ضَبْحاً فَالْمُورِياتِ قَدْحاً فَالْمُغِيراتِ صُبْحاً) The wāw is a particle of oath and genitive; (العاديات) is genitive by the wāw of oath and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted verb of the oath. (ضبحا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, i.e., "they pant a panting", and this implied verb is a ḥāl from (العاديات); it can also be parsed as a ḥāl, i.e., "panting". Al-Khaṭīb said: "The accusative of (ضبحا) is by the implication of a verb, i.e., 'they pant a panting', or by (العاديات), as if it were said 'by the panting ones, panting', because panting occurs only with running; or as ḥāl, i.e., panting." The fāʾ is a conjunction and (الموريات) is conjoined to (العاديات); (قدحا) has the three aspects of (ضبحا). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "(قدحا) is accusative by what (ضبحا) is accusative by." The fāʾ is a conjunction and (المغيرات) is also conjoined to (العاديات); (ضبحا) [Translator's note: the source writes ضبحا here, but the word in the verse is (صبحا)] is accusative as an adverb, i.e., "the ones that raid at the time of morning", and it is attached to (المغيرات). Abū Ḥayyān said, and well: "In this is evidence that these descriptions apply to a single entity, because they are conjoined with the fāʾ, which implies immediate succession. The apparent meaning is that they are the horses on which the disbelieving enemy is fought, and it is not valid to argue that they are camels from the battle of Badr, even though there were only two horsemen in it, since it is not reported that the cause of revelation of this sūra was the battle of Badr; furthermore, it is hardly found that camels were used for jihad in the cause of Allah; rather it is known that jihad in the cause of Allah, the Exalted, is waged only on horses, in the east and west of the lands." He said this in the course of refuting those who interpreted (العاديات) as camels. (فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعاً فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعاً) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (أثرن) is a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, and the nūn is the fāʿil. The conjunction is on a verb, with the active participle's place being replaced, because the meaning is "and those that ran, then struck fire, then raided, then raised". (به) are two elements attached to (أثرن); (نقعا) is a direct object; and the pronoun in (به) refers to the valley, even though it was not mentioned before, which is the place of running; it is also said that it refers to the morning, i.e., "they raised dust in it at the time of morning". Abū Ḥayyān said: "This is better than the first because it is explicitly mentioned." On either interpretation the bāʾ in (به) means "in", and everything that takes "in" can take the bāʾ, but not the reverse. The fāʾ is a conjunction; (وسطن) is a past verb indeclinable on sukūn and the nūn of the feminine plural is the fāʿil; (به) are two elements attached to (وسطن), the pronoun referring to the morning as above or to the dust, in which case the bāʾ is of transitivity, whereas on the first it is locative. It is also said that the bāʾ is a bāʾ of ḥāl, i.e., "they came into the middle accompanied by dust", so it is attached to an omitted element as ḥāl. Abū l-Baqāʾ reported a strange view for which I found no justification, namely that it is redundant, and (جمعا) is the object of (أثرن); and Abū l-Baqāʾ made it stranger still by making it a ḥāl, because he made the bāʾ redundant in the direct object; it is not so. Regrettably Ibn Khālawayh parsed (جمعا) as an adverb, and I do not know, nor does the astrologer know, how that held up for him. (إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ) The clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath. (إن) is a particle resembling the verb; (الإنسان) is its noun; (لربه) are two elements attached to (كنود); the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (كنود) is the khabar of (إن). The alif-lām in (الإنسان) is generic; it is also said to refer to the unbeliever, but the first is preferable, because the nature of man is created that way, calling him to evil, except for whom Allah protects. (وَإِنَّهُ عَلى ذلِكَ لَشَهِيدٌ) Conjoined to the preceding clause, and it is the second thing sworn to. (إن) and its noun; (على ذلك) are two elements attached to (شديد) [Translator's note: the source writes "shadīd" here, but the word in the verse is (شهيد)]; the shifted lām; and (شديد) [sic; (شهيد)] is the khabar of (إن), i.e., he bears witness against himself by what he does, a witness by force that appears in the clear traces of his deeds and their exposing evidences. Al-Zamakhsharī permitted the pronoun to refer to Allah, saying: "It is also said: 'and Allah is, over his ingratitude, a witness', by way of threat." (وَإِنَّهُ لِحُبِّ الْخَيْرِ لَشَدِيدٌ) Conjoined to what precedes, and it is the third thing sworn to. (إن) and its noun; (لحب الخير) are two elements attached to (شديد); the lām is for reinforcement, the meaning being that he is strong and capable in the love of good. One says "he is shadīd for this matter", i.e., capable of it. It is also said that the lām is causal, i.e., "and he, because of the love of wealth, is indeed tight-fisted", and the shifted lām, with (شديد) its khabar. By "good" (khayr) is meant wealth, and the shadīd is the miser, the tight-fisted; one says "so-and-so is shadīd and mutashaddid". Ṭarafa said:
أرى الموت يعتام الكرام ويصطفي ... عقيلة مال الفاحش المتشدّد
(I see death choosing the noble and selecting the choicest of the wealth of the miser, the tight-fisted.)
The wording of Ibn Khālawayh: "Al-khayr here is wealth, as He said, the Exalted: (إن ترك خيرا), i.e., wealth; al-khayr is also horses, in His saying, the Exalted: (إني أحببت حب الخير عن ذكر ربي), meaning horses; and al-khayr is wine: the Arabs say mā ʿindahu khall wa-lā khamr, i.e., neither evil nor good. Al-khayr has the plural khuyūr and al-sharr has shurūr." I say: I did not find in the dictionaries at my disposal this meaning of khayr, i.e., wine, and I would not have recorded this remark, because Ibn Khālawayh is one of the imams attested for retention; but I recorded my remark as a comment on his citing of the proverb. The context in which he cites it indicates that khayr may mean wine, but the proverb certainly does not intend that; rather evil is made vinegar and good wine by way of simile. So their saying in the proverb "he has neither vinegar nor wine" means "he has neither good nor evil", and their saying "you are neither vinegar nor wine" means what al-Maydānī and others pointed out, namely that some Arabs made good "wine" for its pleasantness and evil "vinegar" for its sourness and because a person cannot drink it. (أَفَلا يَعْلَمُ إِذا بُعْثِرَ ما فِي الْقُبُورِ) The hamza is for rebuking interrogation, and the fāʾ is a conjunction on an implied element that the context requires, i.e., "Does he do what he does of vile deeds and not know?" (لا) is negative and (يعلم) is an imperfect verb in the nominative. (إذا) is an adverb for mere time-reference. Zādeh said: "It cannot be an adverb of (يعلم), because knowledge is not what is wanted of man at that time; it is wanted of him while he is in this world. It cannot be an adverb of (بعثر), because the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern the muḍāf; nor of His saying (خبير), because what follows (إن) does not govern what precedes it. So the governing element must be what is indicated by His saying (إن ربهم بهم يومئذ لخبير), i.e., 'Does man not know, in this world, that He, the Exalted, will requite him when it is overturned?' The meaning of Allah's knowledge of them on the Day of Resurrection is His requital of them." The clause (بعثر) is in the position of genitive through the annexation of the adverb to it. (ما) is a relative, the nāʾib fāʿil of (بعثر); (في القبور) are two elements attached to an omitted element with no grammatical position, as the ṣila of (ما). (وَحُصِّلَ ما فِي الصُّدُورِ) Conjoined to (بعثر ما في القبور). (حصل) is a passive past verb, meaning it was gathered in the records and displayed in detail, collected; and it is said: good was distinguished from evil, fat from lean. Zādeh said: "He singled out the deeds of the hearts for mention and omitted the deeds of the limbs, because they follow the deeds of the hearts; for were the motives and intentions not realised in the hearts, the acts of the limbs would not come about." This is a good statement, so ponder it. (إِنَّ رَبَّهُمْ بِهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَخَبِيرٌ) The clause is a justification for the omitted governor of (إذا), which is the object of (يعلم), i.e., "Does he not know that We will requite him at the time mentioned?" Then He justified that by His saying "Indeed their Lord..." etc. (إن) and its noun; (بهم) are two elements attached to (خبير); (يومئذ) is an adverb also attached to (خبير); the shifted lām; and (خبير) is the khabar of (إن).

* Rhetoric:
1- In the difference between the conjoined and the thing it is conjoined to in His saying «فأثرن به نقعا», in that a verb is conjoined to the noun that is (العاديات) and what follows it — because those are active participles that give the meaning of a verb — there is a wonderful secret: the depiction of these actions in the soul and their embodiment before the eye. For depiction is achieved by bringing a verb after a noun, because of the contrast between them, and it is more eloquent than depiction and embodiment by harmonious nouns. Likewise the depiction by an imperfect after a past, for which there have been examples, the closest being the saying of ʿAmr ibn Maʿdī Karib:
بأني قد لقيت الغول تهوي ... بسهب كالصحيفة صحصحان
فأضربها بلا دهش فخرت ... صريعا لليدين وللجران
(That I met the ghoul swooping down upon a plain like a sheet, level and open; / I struck her without bewilderment, and she fell, prostrate on her hands and her neck.)
2- In His saying «فالموريات قدحا» there is a metaphor for the horses kindling war; it is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya): war is likened to a blazing fire, the likened is omitted and the likened-to is retained. The Exalted said: (كلما أوقدوا نارا للحرب أطفأها الله), and it is said "ḥamiya l-waṭīs" (the oven grew hot) when war intensifies.
3- In His saying «إن ربهم بهم يومئذ لخبير» there is tajnīs al-taḥrīf (paronomasia of altered vowelling), which some call "al-jinās al-muḥarraf", which is where the vowel-pointing is what distinguishes the two words or parts of them; it is also what has its two members agreeing in number of letters and differing in vowels, whether they are from two nouns, two verbs, a noun and a verb, or other. The utmost of it is His saying, the Exalted: (ولقد أرسلنا فيهم منذرين، فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المنذرين). It is not said that the two words are identical in meaning so that there is no paronomasia between them, because we say that the first is meant as active participle and the second as passive participle, so the difference is clear. Of it is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "O Allah, as You have made my khalq (form) good, make my khuluq (character) good", and similar to it their saying jubbat al-burd, junnat al-burd, and their saying raṭib al-ruṭab, ḍarb min al-ḍarb. Of poetry is the saying of Abū Tammām:
هنّ الحمام فإن كسرت عيافة ... من خائهنّ فإنهنّ حمام
(They are doves [ḥamām]; if you break off the omen-reading from their "khāʾ", then they are death [ḥimām].) [Translator's note: the rendering of this verse is tentative.]
and similarly the saying of al-Maʿarrī:
والحسن يظهر في شيئين رونقه ... بيت من الشعر أو بيت من الشعر
(Beauty shows its brilliance in two things: a house of hair [a tent] or a verse of poetry.)
and from him also:
لغيري زكاة من جمال فإن تكن ... زكاة جمال فاذكري ابن سبيل
(For others the alms [tax] of beauty; if there is an alms of beauty, then remember the wayfarer.)
4- In His saying «وإنه على ذلك لشهيد وإنه لحب الخير لشديد» there is al-jinās al-lāḥiq, which is where one of its two members has one letter replaced by another not of the same articulation point, whether the replacement is at the beginning, middle or end; if what is replaced is of the same articulation point it is called muḍāriʿ. An example of replacement at the beginning is His saying, the Exalted: (ويل لكل همزة لمزة); the verse we are on is an example of replacement in the middle; and an example of replacement at the end is His saying, the Exalted: (وإذا جاءهم أمر من الأمن). Among ḥadīths of this type, from the beginning is his saying, peace be upon him: "Praise be to Allah who made my form good and adorned in me what disfigured in others"; from the second, the ḥadīth of al-Ṭabarānī, "Were it not for bowing men, suckling infants and grazing beasts"; and from the third, also al-Ṭabarānī's ḥadīth, "My community will not perish until there appear among them al-tamāyuz and al-tamāyul", and al-Daylamī's ḥadīth, "The most beloved of believers to Allah is the one who devotes himself to obedience to Allah and gives sincere counsel to the community of Muḥammad". Among poetic examples in the same order, also, is the saying of Abū Firās:
إن الغني هو الغني بنفسه ... ولو أنه عاري المناكب حافي
ما كل ما فوق البسيطة كافيا ... وإذا قنعت فكل شيء كافي
(True wealth is wealth of the self, even if one is bare-shouldered and barefoot. Not everything on the face of the earth suffices; but when you are content, everything suffices.)
and from the second, the saying of al-Buḥturī:
وقعودي عن التقلب والأر ... ض لمثلي رحيبة الأكناف
ليس عن ثروة بلغت مداها ... غير أنّي امرؤ كفاني كفافي
(My sitting back from roving, though the earth is wide-flanked for one like me, is not from wealth that has reached its limit, but because I am a man whom my sufficiency suffices.)
and from the third, the saying of one of them:
شوقي لذاك المحيا الزاهر الزاهي ... شوق شديد وجسمي الواهن الواهي
أسهرت طرفي وولهت الفؤاد هوى ... فالقلب والطرف بين الساهر الساهي
(My longing for that radiant, shining face is intense longing, and my body is weak and frail. Love has kept my eye awake and driven my heart distraught; so heart and eye are between one wakeful and one heedless.)

farraa:1-1.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلْعَادِيَاتِ ضَبْحاً﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: They are the horses, and «الضبح» is the sounds of their breathing when they run. He said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us; he said: Ḥibbān narrated that to me with his chain of transmission from Ibn ʿAbbās. [Translator's note: the source has «والضبيح: أصواتٍ أنفاسها»; translated as «الضبح» and «أصوات», as the context requires.]

farraa:2-2.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱلمُورِيَاتِ قَدْحاً﴾.
They strike fire with their hooves; it is the fire of al-Ḥubāḥib. Al-Kalbī said, with his chain of transmission: al-Ḥubāḥib was [a man] of one of the tribes of the Arabs, and he was among the most miserly of people. His miserliness reached the point that he would light a fire only at night, and if someone woke up to take a light from it, he would put it out. Likewise the fire that the horses strike is of no use, just as the fire of al-Ḥubāḥib is of no use.

farraa:3-3.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱلْمُغِيرَاتِ صُبْحاً﴾.
The horses raided at dawn. It was a raiding party that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent to Banū Kināna, and news of it was slow in reaching him; so revelation came down to him with news of it in «العاديات». ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah have mercy on him, used to say: they are the camels, and he took it to refer to the battle of Badr, and said: We had with us that day only one horse, on which was al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad.

farraa:4-4.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعاً﴾.
«النقع» is dust; and it is also said: earth.
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بِهِ نَقْعاً﴾: He means [146/b] by «به» the valley, though He did not mention it before that. This is permissible, because dust is only raised from some place, even if it is not mentioned; and when the name of a thing is known, it may be referred to by a pronoun even if no mention of it has occurred.
Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ فِى لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ﴾, meaning the Qurʾān, and it is the opening of a surah; and opening a surah with it is no different from mentioning it in a verse after it has been mentioned in what precedes, as in His word: ﴿حم، والكِتَابِ الْمُبِينِ، إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ﴾. And Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿إِنِّى أَحْبَبْتُ حُبَّ الْخَيْرِ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّى حتَّى تَوَارَتْ بِالحِجَابِ﴾, meaning the sun, though no mention of it had occurred.

farraa:5-5.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعاً﴾.
They agreed on the light form, without shadda, (فوسطن); had it been read "فوسّطن", it would have been correct, because the Arabs say: وسَطت الشىء, ووسَّطته, and توسَّطته, with one meaning (I got into the middle of the thing).

farraa:6-6.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ﴾.
Al-Kalbī said — and he claimed that it is in the dialect of Kinda and Ḥaḍramawt — "لَكَنُود": ungrateful indeed for blessings.
Al-Ḥasan said: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ﴾: he said: reproachful of his Lord, counting misfortunes and forgetting blessings.

farraa:7-7.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ عَلَىٰ ذَلِكَ لَشَهِيدٌ﴾.
He says: and Allah is a witness to that.

farraa:8-8.t:
His words, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لِحُبِّ ٱلْخَيْرِ لَشَدِيدٌ﴾.
There has been disagreement about this. Al-Kalbī said, with his chain of transmission: «لشديد» means: miserly indeed. Another said: and he, for love of wealth, is strong indeed; and «الخير» is wealth. We consider — and Allah knows best — that the meaning is: وإنه لِلْخير لشديد الحب (and he is intense in love for wealth); and «الخير» is wealth. It is as though, since «الحب» came first in the expression, and its [proper] place was for «شديد» to be annexed to it, «الحب» was dropped from the end because mention of it had occurred at the beginning, and [also] for the verse-endings. Similar to it in Sūrat Ibrāhīm is: ﴿أَعْمَالُهُمْ كَرَمَادٍ اشْتَدَّتْ بِهِ الرِّيحُ فِى يَوْمٍ عَاصِفٍ﴾; storminess does not belong to days, it belongs only to the wind; [147/a] but since mention of the wind had occurred before «اليوم», it was dropped from its end, as though it were said: فى يوم عاصف الريح (on a day stormy of wind).

farraa:9-9.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَلاَ يَعْلَمُ إِذَا بُعْثِرَ مَا فِي ٱلْقُبُورِ﴾.
I saw it in the muṣḥaf of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] as: "إذا بحث ما فى القبور". And I heard one of the Bedouins of Banū Asad recite it, and he said: "بحثر". They are two dialects: بحثر and بعثر.

farraa:10-10.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَحُصِّلَ مَا فِي ٱلصُّدُورِ﴾: made clear.

farraa:11-11.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّهُم بِهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَّخَبِيرٌ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is: "بأنه يومئذ بهم خبير".

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «ضبحًا»: nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq (substitute for the absolute object) that meets its governing word «العاديات» in meaning, for الضَّبْح (panting) is a kind of going and running.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: His saying «فالموريات»: a noun conjoined to «العاديات»; «قدحًا»: nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq (substitute for the absolute object) that meets its governing word «الموريات» in meaning, because kindling (الإيراء) comes from striking (القدح).

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «صبحًا»: an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «المغيرات».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The clause «فأثرن» is conjoined to the single word «المغيرات», in the position of the genitive; the preposition «به» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: (إن الإنسان لربه لكنود) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam); the preposition «لربه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «كنود».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: (وإنه على ذلك لشهيد) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The preposition «على ذلك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «شهيد».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: (وإنه لحب الخير لشديد) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The preposition «لحب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «شديد».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The clause is resumptive; «إذا»: an adverb stripped of the conditional sense, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what the khabar (predicate) of إن indicates, i.e.: when it is scattered, they will be recompensed; «ما»: a relative noun, nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: (إن ربهم بهم يومئذ لخبير) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause stands in place of the two objects of {يَعْلَمُ}, and the hamza of «إنَّ» takes kasra because of the lām coming in the khabar (predicate). The preposition «بهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خبير», and the adverb is attached to «خبير».

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He (ضبحا): a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), like «أصبح ماؤكم غورا».

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying (قدحا): a pure maṣdar (verbal noun) [i.e. a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)], because (فالموريات) means «فالقادحات» (those that strike sparks). [Translator's note: the bracketed gloss is added for clarity.]

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying (صبحا): an adverb of time, governed by (المغيرات).

mekki-muskil:4-4.t: His saying (نقعا): a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), made accusative by (أثرن).

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying (إذا بعثر): the governing word (ʿāmil) in (إذا), according to al-Mubarrad, is (بعثر). Neither (يعلم) nor (خبير) governs it, because knowledge and taking heed are not what is required of man at that time; one takes heed only in this world. And as for (يعلم): what comes after (إنّ) does not govern what precedes it. [Translator's note: the source text here reads «ويعلم ولا يعمل ما بعد إن فيما قبلها», which is somewhat disjointed; it has been rendered according to its evident sense.] Were you to say «يوم الجمعة إن زيدا قائم», it would not be permissible except as two separate utterances, with an ʿāmil implied for (يوم), as though you said «اذكر يوم الجمعة» (remember Friday) and then said «إن زيدا قائم»; and (قائم) can in no way govern it. As for the second (يومئذ), the governing word in it is (خبير). It is permissible for what comes after the lām to govern what precedes it [Translator's note: the printed text has «ابعد اللام», read as «ما بعد اللام»], because the lām is, in the implied structure, meant to be at the mubtadaʾ (subject); it entered the khabar (predicate) only because (إنّ) entered upon the mubtadaʾ. So the khabar governs what precedes it, even though it contains a lām, according to the original rule of the lām, which in the implied structure is before the mubtadaʾ.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿والعاديات﴾: the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, and «العاديات» is a noun genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of oath, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb of oath.
﴿ضبحا﴾: standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, because «الضبح» is a kind of travelling and running. Or: a mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative by the fatḥa, of an omitted verb, i.e. «يضبحن ضبحا» ("panting a panting"), and the implied clause ﴿يضبحن ضبحا﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «العاديات». Or ﴿ضبحًا﴾ is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. "panting" (ضابحاتٍ), or "possessed of panting" (ذوي ضَبْح). «الضبح» is a sound heard from the chests of horses when running. The oath clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿فالموريات﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «الموريات» is conjoined to ﴿العاديات﴾, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿قدحا﴾: standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa. Or: a mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative by the fatḥa, of an omitted verb, i.e. «يقدحن قدحا» ("striking sparks a striking"), and the implied clause ﴿يقدحن قدحا﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الموريات». Or ﴿قدحًا﴾ is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. "striking sparks" (قادحاتٍ).

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿فالمغيرات﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «المغيرات» is conjoined to ﴿الموريات﴾, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿صبحا﴾: an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿المغيرات﴾.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿فأثرن﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «أثرن» is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and the nūn is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿به﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the kasra in the position of genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أثرن﴾, and the pronoun in ﴿به﴾ refers back to the morning, or to the place of the raid, or to the running.
﴿نقعا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa; the clause ﴿أثرن﴾ has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the active participle before it, because that participle is interpreted as a verb, since it occurs as the ṣila of ﴿أل﴾, i.e. ﴿واللاتي عدون فأورين فأغرن فأثرن﴾ ("by those that ran, then struck sparks, then raided, then raised").

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿فوسطن﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «وسطن» is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and the nūn is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿به﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the kasra in the position of genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿وسطن﴾. The pronoun in ﴿به﴾ refers back to the morning, so the bāʾ is adverbial (ẓarfiyya); or to the dust, so the bāʾ is for transitivity, i.e. "they placed the dust (النقع), which is the «الغبار», in the midst of the host"; or the bāʾ is circumstantial, i.e. "they penetrated into the midst, enveloped in dust", so the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to something omitted, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of ﴿فوسطن﴾.
﴿جمعا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa; the clause ﴿وسطن﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿أثرن﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, with no grammatical position.
﴿الإنسان﴾: the noun (ism) of «إن», accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿لربه﴾: the lām is a preposition, and «رب» is a noun genitive (majrūr) by the lām, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; «رب» is muḍāf, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the kasra in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كنود﴾.
﴿لكنود﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and «كنود» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن», nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma; the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the answer of the oath.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿وإنه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «إن» is an abrogating particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, with no grammatical position, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of accusative as the noun (ism) of «إن».
﴿على ذلك﴾: «على» is a preposition, and «ذا» is a demonstrative indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of genitive; the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿شهيد﴾.
﴿لشهيد﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and «شهيد» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن», nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma. The clause ﴿إنه على ذلك...﴾ has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the preceding clause that answers the oath.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿وإنه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «إن» is an abrogating particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, with no grammatical position, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of accusative as the noun (ism) of «إن».
﴿لحب﴾: the lām is a preposition, and «حب» is a noun genitive (majrūr) by the lām, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿شديد﴾, and «حب» is muḍāf.
﴿الخير﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive by the kasra.
﴿لشديد﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and «شديد» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن», nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma; the clause ﴿وإنه لحب الخير...﴾ has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause answering the oath ﴿إن الإنسان...﴾.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿أفلا يعلم﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (inkārī), a particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa with no grammatical position; the fāʾ conjoins to something implied, i.e. "does he do the vile things he does, and does he not know?" (أيفعل ما يفعل من القبائح فلا يعلم); «لا» is negating; and «يعلم» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو), referring back to man; the object of «يعلم» is omitted, i.e. "does he not know that We will requite him?" (أفلا يعلم أنا نجازيه).
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb of future time stripped of the sense of condition, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied object of «يعلم», i.e. "does he not know that We will requite him when what is in the graves is scattered..." (أفلا يعلم أنا نجازيه إذا بعثر...إلخ).
﴿بعثر﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and it is passive (lit. "whose agent is not named").
﴿ما﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of «بعثر».
﴿في القبور﴾: «في» is a preposition, and «القبور» is a noun genitive (majrūr) by «في», the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to something omitted that is the ṣila (relative clause), and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. The clause ﴿بعثر ما في القبور﴾ is in the position of genitive by the adverb being annexed to it.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿وحصل﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «حُصِّلَ» is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and it is passive (lit. "whose agent is not named").
﴿ما﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of «حصِّل».
﴿في الصدور﴾: «في» is a preposition, and «الصدور» is a noun genitive (majrūr) by «في», the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted that is the ṣila (relative clause), and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. The clause ﴿حصل ما في الصدور﴾ is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause ﴿بعثر ما في القبور﴾.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, with no grammatical position.
﴿ربهم﴾: the noun (ism) of «إن», accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa; «رب» is muḍāf, the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and the mīm is the sign of the plural.
﴿بهم﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the kasra in the position of genitive, and the mīm is the sign of the plural; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خبير﴾.
﴿يومئذ﴾: «يوم» is an adverb of time, accusative by the fatḥa, attached to ﴿خبير﴾, and it is muḍāf; «إذٍ» is a noun indeclinable on the sukūn, implied because the place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, i.e. "on the day when what is in the graves is scattered and what is in the breasts is brought out" (يوم إذ يُبعثَر ما في القبور ويُحَصَّل ما في الصدور).
﴿لخبير﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and «خبير» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن», nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma; the clause gives the reason for the omitted object of ﴿يعلم﴾, with no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:1-5.t:
فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعاً (5)
وَالْعادِياتِ is genitive by the wāw of oath. The scholars have two views on its meaning. Mujāhid and ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that it is the horses; and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: it is the camels, and Ibn Masʿūd said the same. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: A man asked me about وَالْعادِياتِ ضَبْحاً (1), and I said: it is the horses. He went to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and informed him, and he sent for me and had me brought, and said to me: "Do you speak about the Book of Allah without knowledge? By Allah, the first expedition was Badr, and we had only two horses with us: a horse of al-Zubayr and a horse of al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad. The runners (al-ʿādiyāt) are only from ʿArafa to al-Muzdalifa, and from al-Muzdalifa to Minā."
A parallel to this is what al-Buhlūl ibn Isḥāq ibn al-Buhlūl ibn Ḥassān narrated to us: Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways narrated to us: Kathīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Muzanī narrated to us, saying: I was with Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī, and a man came to him and said: "O Abū Ḥamza, I am a man who has never performed the pilgrimage (ṣarūra); I have never made the Ḥajj, so teach me some of what Allah, Glorified, has taught you." He said: "Do you read the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then begin, and read بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ, five verses: وَالْعادِياتِ ضَبْحاً (1) فَالْمُورِياتِ قَدْحاً (2) فَالْمُغِيراتِ صُبْحاً (3) فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعاً (4) فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعاً (5). Do you know what this is?" He said: "No." He said: "«والعاديات ضبحا» is the departure from ʿArafa; فَالْمُورِياتِ قَدْحاً (2) is to al-Muzdalifa; فَالْمُغِيراتِ صُبْحاً (3): they do not press on until morning; فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعاً (4) فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعاً (5) is the day of Minā."
Abū Jaʿfar said: The scholars disagreed on the meaning of فَالْمُورِياتِ قَدْحاً. The position of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and Ibn Masʿūd is that it is the camels. Mujāhid and ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: (it is) people kindling fire so that others may see it. Others narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: the horses. Qatāda said: the horses kindle war. ʿIkrima said: al-mūriyāt are the tongues. Abū Jaʿfar said: There is no evidence indicating that any of these views should be specified, so the correct thing is to say that it applies to everyone who kindles, given that the meaning is one, the implied form being "by the Lord of the runners".
ضَبْحاً was put in the accusative because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). From Ibn ʿAbbās: al-ḍabḥ is their blowing through their lips. قَدْحاً was put in the accusative as a maṣdar, because the meaning of «فالموريات» is "those that strike sparks (al-qādiḥāt)". «فالمغيرات»: from Ibn ʿAbbās, that it is the horses, and from Ibn Masʿūd, that it is the camels. «ضبحا» [Translator's note: so in the text; evidently صُبْحاً is meant] is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعاً (4): al-Farrāʾ said: the hāʾ is a pronoun for the valley, which has not been mentioned before, because the meaning is known. Abū al-Jawzāʾ narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: al-naqʿ is the dust. Wasaṭna, wassaṭna and tawassaṭna are one (in meaning).

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: He says: (حُصِّلَ means) brought out into the open.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: «إنّ» took kasra because of the lām. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān reported from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that it is permissible to give it fatḥa together with the lām, because it (the lām) is redundant (zāʾida): its entering is like its leaving, except that it conveys emphasis.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: The exegetes hold that its meaning is "ungrateful", i.e., ungrateful for His favours. Al-Ḥasan said: he is resentful toward his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and blames Him for the afflictions that befall him, and forgets the favours.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: وَإِنَّهُ, i.e., and his Lord, عَلى ذلِكَ لَشَهِيدٌ.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: وَإِنَّهُ, i.e., and man, لِحُبِّ الْخَيْرِ لَشَدِيدٌ: there are several views on its meaning. It has been said: (he is) of intense strength. The view of al-Farrāʾ is that the meaning is that man is intense in love of good; so the implied form according to him is "he, in love of good, is intense in love", then what came after شديد was omitted. The third view — I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: (it is) as you say "I honour so-and-so for you", i.e., for your sake; i.e., and he, for the sake of love of good, i.e., wealth, is "intense", i.e., miserly.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: It is not permissible for «يعلم» to govern «إذا», nor «لخبير»; rather the operator in it according to Muḥammad ibn Yazīd is «بعثر». And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās. [Translator's note: the entry breaks off here; the report continues in the next entry.]

safi-cedvel:9-11.t:
* I'rab:
(the fāʾ) is a conjunction, and the interrogative is one of denial. (لا) is negative. (إذا) is an adverb in the position of the accusative, stripped of the conditional sense [Note: or containing the sense of a condition.], attached to an omitted element which is explained by His saying, the Exalted: إنّ ربّهم ... خبير, i.e. "Allah knows them" [Note: or attached to the implied object of يعلم, the clause إنّ ربّهم.. being a justification of that object, i.e.: does man not know that We shall requite him at the time the graves are scattered, because their Lord is well-acquainted with them? And if the adverb contains the sense of a condition, it is attached to the implied apodosis that is justified by His saying: إنّ ربّهم.., i.e. when what is in the graves is scattered, their recompense is completed according to their deeds, because their Lord is well-acquainted with them.], (في القبور) is attached to an omitted element, the ṣila (relative clause) of the first ما; (في الصدور) is the ṣila of the second ما; (بهم) is attached to (خبير), and likewise (يومئذ), the adverb which is accusative – or indeclinable (mabnī); (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) of emphasis..
Clause: «يعلم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e.: does he commit vile deeds and so not know that We shall requite him on the Day of Resurrection?
And the clause: «بعثر ... » is in the position of genitive, as muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «حصّل ... » is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause بعثر.
And the clause: «إنّ ربّهم بهم ... لخبير» has no grammatical position; it is a justification of the implied object [Note: or it is the object of يعلم, and the hamza of (إنّ) was given a kasra because of the lām in the predicate, though it should properly have a fatḥa.].

* Rhetoric:
Tajnīs al-taḥrīf (paronomasia by vocalization): in His saying, the Exalted: «إِنَّ رَبَّهُمْ بِهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَخَبِيرٌ».
This is the art in which the vocalization is what distinguishes the two words or some of their letters; it is also the case where the two members agree in the number of letters and differ in the vowels, whether they are two nouns, two verbs, a noun and a verb, or something else.

* Benefits:
- Depiction in the Noble Qur'an:
Among the secrets of inimitability in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is that it depicts meanings and ideas magnificently and embodies them as if they were a moving life passing before us, which our senses, our thought and our imagination take in; in addition to this, the words, by their sound and rhythm, help to draw the picture and give it its dimensions. This sūra is of that kind. At its opening it drew for us the picture of the raiding horses hastening to jihad, and the expression came depicting and bringing out that picture. Let us imagine these two verbal nouns with their rhythm and sound (ضبحا، قدحا): they depict the vehemence of the horses hastening to jihad; and the use of the following attributes (العاديات - الموريات - المغيرات) completes the picture and gives it its inner and psychological dimension. In His saying, the Exalted: (فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعاً. فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعاً) the picture is completed, and we sense movement and life flowing through this wonderful expression. From the harmony of expression in this sūra, we noticed how its opening is marked by short verse-endings and an intensity of expression that suits the picture of the horses, the melee and the dust. In its second part, when it turns to express man's ingratitude and his love of wealth, the expression calms down and lengthens, to suit the situation (إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ، وَإِنَّهُ عَلى ذلِكَ لَشَهِيدٌ. وَإِنَّهُ لِحُبِّ الْخَيْرِ لَشَدِيدٌ), then it returns to fit the scene of the Resurrection and the reckoning. We also notice that the verbs, by their sound, draw the scene of the Resurrection and its violence: (أَفَلا يَعْلَمُ إِذا بُعْثِرَ ما فِي الْقُبُورِ وَحُصِّلَ ما فِي الصُّدُورِ). The verb (بعثر) expresses the violence of the Resurrection and the severity of the matter, and (حصّل) expresses gathering out with force. Hence we note the precision in using the verb so as to express the required meaning with utmost exactness, and we note the movement and life that flow through the words of the Noble Qur'an; and this is one of the secrets of inimitability in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

safi-cedvel:1-8.t:
* I'rab:
(والعاديات) is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم ("I swear") (ضبحا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, its implied form being تضبح [Note: or a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar because of its meeting it in meaning, since the racing horses are panting, or a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl: panting.], (الفاء) is a conjunction in the four places (قدحا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, its implied form being تقدح [Note: the two aspects mentioned for (ضبحا) are permissible in it.], (صبحا) is an accusative adverb of time attached to (المغيرات), (به) is attached to (أثرن) [Note: to the place of their running or to that time.], and the second to (وسطن) [Note: the pronoun in (به) refers to the morning or to the dust; it is possible that the prepositional phrase is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of وسطن: "clothed in the dust".], (جمعا) is an accusative mafʿūl bihi (لربّه) is attached to (كنود), (اللام) is the shifted lām — or the lām of oath — (الواو) is a conjunction in both places (على ذلك) is attached to (شهيد) (اللام) is like the first in both places (لحبّ) is attached to (شديد) [Note: and the lām is for reinforcement or for causation.] ..
Clause: « (أقسم) بالعاديات ... » has no grammatical position; it is an opening clause.
And the clause: «أثرن ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to (مغيرات), because it stands in the position of the ṣila of the relative (ال), i.e.: "those who raided ... and raised".
And the clause: «وسطن» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أثرن.
And the clause: «إنّ الإنسان ... لكنود» has no grammatical position; it is the jawāb al-qasam.
And the clause: «إنّه ... لشهيد» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the answer to the oath.
And the clause: «إنّه ... لشديد» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the answer to the oath.

* Morphology:
(1) العاديات: plural of العادية, feminine of العادي, an active participle from عدا meaning "ran"; its pattern is فاعل, and it contains an ʿilāl by substitution; its origin is العادو, the wāw, vowelled after a kasra, was changed to yāʾ..
(ضبحا): the maṣdar of the triliteral ضبحت الخيل تضبح, of the bāb of فتح, i.e. they made a sound that is neither neighing nor snorting; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(2) الموريات: plural of المورية, feminine of الموري, an active participle from أورى النار, when he struck stones to bring fire out of them; its pattern is مفعل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(قدحا): a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral قدح الحجارة ببعضها, of the bāb of فتح, when he struck them to bring out fire; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(3) المغيرات: plural of المغيرة, feminine of المغير, an active participle from the quadriliteral (أغار); its pattern is مفعل, taking into account the ʿilāl by quiescence — making the yāʾ quiescent and moving its vowel to the ghayn before it — (4) نقعا: a noun meaning dust; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(6) كنود: an intensive form from (كند) النعمة, i.e. he was ungrateful for the blessing, of the bāb of نصر; its pattern is فعول, for masculine and feminine.

* Rhetoric:
Explicit metaphor: in His saying, the Exalted «فَالْمُورِياتِ قَدْحاً».
A metaphor for horses kindling and igniting the fire of war: war is likened to a blazing fire, the thing likened was dropped and the thing likened to was kept.
Difference between the conjoined and the thing conjoined to: in His saying, the Exalted «فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعاً».
Here a verb is conjoined to a noun, namely العاديات and what follows it; in reality the conjunction is to the verb in whose place the active participle was put, since the meaning is: "those that ran, then struck fire, then raided, then raised".
Annexed paronomasia (al-jinās al-lāḥiq): in His saying, the Exalted «وَإِنَّهُ عَلى ذلِكَ لَشَهِيدٌ وَإِنَّهُ لِحُبِّ الْخَيْرِ لَشَدِيدٌ».
This paronomasia is that in which one of the two pillars is replaced by one letter with another from a different articulation point, whether the replacement is at the beginning, middle or end. The verse we are dealing with is an example of replacement in the middle.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {إِنَّ الإنسان}: this is the thing sworn upon (al-muqsam ʿalayhi). «لرَبَّه» is attached to the khabar (predicate), and it was placed first for the sake of the verse-endings (fawāṣil). Al-kanūd means the ungrateful (al-jaḥūd). It was also said: the one who is ungrateful for blessings (al-kafūr li-l-niʿma), and the following was recited:
4628 - كَنُوْدٌ لِنَعْماءِ الرجالِ ومَنْ يَكُنْ ... كَنُوْداً لِنَعْماءِ الرجالِ يُبَعَّدِ
(Ungrateful for the favours of men; and whoever is ungrateful for the favours of men will be kept far away.)
It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: in the dialect of Kinda and Ḥaḍramawt it means the disobedient; in the dialect of Rabīʿa and Muḍar, the ungrateful (kafūr); and in the dialect of Kināna, the miserly. Abū Zayd recited:
4629 - إنْ تَفْتْني فلم أَطِبْ عنك نَفْساً ... غيرَ أنِّي أمنى بدَيْنٍ كَنُودِ
(If you slip away from me, I will not find my heart at ease about you, except that I am afflicted with an ungrateful debt.)

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {لِحُبِّ}: the lām is attached to «شديدٌ», and there are two possibilities in it. The first: that it is the lām that makes the verb transitive (al-muʿaddiya). The meaning is then: "and he is strong, able to bear the love of good (wealth)". One says "he is shadīd for this matter", that is, able to bear it. The second: that it expresses cause (li-l-ʿilla), that is: "and because of his love of wealth he is truly miserly". It was also said that the lām has the meaning of «على» ("upon"), but there is no need for that. "Strong" (shadīd) and "stern" (mutashaddid) can be used to mean "miserly". The poet said:
4630 - [أرى] الموتَ يَعْتامُ الكرامَ ويَصْطَفي ... عَقيلةَ مالِ الفاحشِ المتشدِّدِ
(I see death choosing out the noble, and picking the choicest of the wealth of the shameless, miserly man.)
Al-Farrāʾ said: "The original arrangement of the verse would be to say: «وإنه لشديدُ الحُبِّ للخير» ("and he is intense in love of good"). But when he put «الحُبّ» first he said «لشديد», and omitted at its end the mention of «الحُبِّ», because it had already been mentioned, and for the sake of the verse-endings, as in His saying: {فِي يَوْمٍ عَاصِفٍ} [Ibrāhīm: 18], where 'blustery' (al-ʿuṣūf) belongs to the wind and not to the day, as if He had said: 'on a day of blustery wind'."

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {إِذَا بُعْثِرَ}: there are several views on what governs «إذا». The first: «بُعْثِرَ» itself; Makkī transmitted this from al-Mubarrad, and the verification of it was given shortly before, in the sūra preceding this one. The second: that it is what the khabar of «إنَّ» indicates, that is: "when it is turned over (buʿthira), they will be recompensed". The third: that it is «يَعْلَمُ»; al-Ḥawfī and Abū l-Baqāʾ held this. Makkī rejected it, saying: "Because the human being is not required to know and take heed at that time; he takes heed and knows only in this world." Al-Shaykh said: "It is not clear, because the meaning is: does he not know now?"
He had said before that: "The object (mafʿūl) of «يَعْلَمُ» is omitted, and it is what governs the adverbial (al-ẓarf), that is: does he not know his ultimate fate when it is turned over?" End of quotation. He thus made it transitive, by the apparent sense of his words, to one object. On this basis it may be said that it governs «إذا» in the sense that «إذا» is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) and not an adverbial, since the implied sense is: "does he not know the time of the overturning of the graves?", meaning that he should acknowledge the resurrection and its time. «إذا» has indeed been used with a shift of function and has left adverbial use, and there are witnesses for that which were mentioned in the course of this work. The fourth: that what governs it is omitted, and it is the object of «يَعْلَمُ», as already explained, that is: "he knows his ultimate fate when it is turned over". It is not permissible that «لَخبيرٌ» govern it, because what is within the scope of «إنَّ» cannot precede it.
The majority read «بُعْثِرَ» with ʿayn, in the passive; the relative noun (al-mawṣūl) stands in the place of the agent (nāʾib al-fāʿil). Ibn Masʿūd read it with ḥāʾ. Al-Aswad ibn Yazīd and Muḥammad ibn Maʿdān read «بُحِثَ», from "searching" (al-baḥth). Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim read «بَعْثَرَ» in the active, the agent being Allah the Exalted or the angel. The majority read «حُصِّل» in the passive, like the preceding one. Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar, Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim and Ibn Maʿdān read «حَصَّلَ» in the active. It is also reported from Ibn Yaʿmar and Naṣr: «حَصَلَ», with ṣād unshaddened, in the active, in the sense "he gathered what was in the scrolls (al-ṣuḥuf) by collecting". Taḥṣīl is the gathering of a thing, and ḥuṣūl is its coming together. It was also said that taḥṣīl is discrimination (al-tamyīz); from it the sieve is called muḥaṣṣil. And «ḥaṣala» (unshaddened) of a thing means: it appeared and became clear, and the last reading rests on this.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {إِنَّ رَبَّهُم}: the majority read with kasra on the hamza, because of the presence of the lām in its khabar. The apparent sense is that it is suspended (muʿallaqa) from «يَعْلَمُ», so it is in the position of the accusative (fī maḥall naṣb); but its khabar does not govern «إذا», for the reason given above; rather, a governor is implied for it, drawn from its meaning, as already explained. What shows that it is a suspender of the knowing and not resumptive (mustaʾnifa) is the reading of Abū l-Sammāl and others, «أنَّ ربَّهم بهم يؤمئذٍ خبيرٌ», with fatḥa and with the lām omitted, for in this reading it fills the place of the two objects of the verb. It is related of the wicked-spirited al-Ḥajjāj that when he put fatḥa on the hamza of «أنَّ», he corrected himself and deliberately dropped the lām. If that is sound, it is disbelief (kufr). It may not be said that this is an established reading, as I reported it from Abū l-Sammāl, and so he would not be a disbeliever; for if he had read it so as one transmitting it, he would not have been forbidden; rather, he dropped the lām deliberately in order to set his own tongue right. The Community is agreed that whoever adds a letter to the Qurʾān or removes one deliberately is a disbeliever. I have said this only because I saw that the Shaykh said: "Abū l-Sammāl and al-Ḥajjāj read it", whereas nothing is preserved from al-Ḥajjāj except this evil report, which people transmit from him in this form; and he is too insignificant for it to be transmitted from him.
«بهم» and «يومئذٍ» are both attached to the khabar, and the lām is no obstacle to that; they were put first for the sake of the verse-ending (fāṣila).

[Translator's note: the source prints «وإساقطِ اللامِ» ("and the dropping of the lām" is the evident sense); translated as the evident sense.]

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {والعاديات}: the plural of «عادِيَة», which is the one running swiftly, from العَدْو, which is going swiftly. The yāʾ is from a wāw because of the kasra before it, like الغازِيات from الغَزْو. One says: عَدا يَعْدو عَدْواً, so he is عادٍ and she is عادِيَة. This has already been discussed in [Sūrat] al-Muʾminūn.
His saying: {ضَبْحاً}: There are several views on it. The first: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) emphasising the active participle; for الضَّبْح is a kind of going and running, like الضَّبْع. One says: ضَبَحَ الفَرَسُ and ضَبَعَ when it runs hard, taken from الضَّبْع, which is the foreleg, because it stretches it out when running; it is as though the ḥāʾ were a substitute for the ʿayn. Abū ʿUbayda and al-Mubarrad held this; they said: الضَّبْح is from their stretching [their forelegs] in going. ʿAntara said:
4617 - والخيلُ تعلَمُ حين تَضْ ... بَحُ في حِياضِ المَوْتِ ضَبْحاً
(And the horses know, when they run panting in the pools of death…)
The second: it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. panting, or possessing panting. الضَّبْح is a sound heard from the chests of horses when running, which is not neighing. From Ibn ʿAbbās: he imitated it, saying: «أحْ أحْ». It is transmitted from him that no animal pants (yaḍbaḥ) except horses, dogs and foxes. This ought not to be authentic from him, for it is related that he said: «I was asked about it and I explained it as horses. ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, was beneath the watering-place of Zamzam; [the man] asked him and mentioned to him what I had said. So he summoned me, and when I stood over him he said: "You give people legal opinions without knowledge! It was the first expedition in Islam, namely Badr, and we had only two horses: a horse of al-Miqdād and a horse of al-Zubayr. «والعاديات ضَبْحاً» are the camels [running] from ʿArafa to al-Muzdalifa and from al-Muzdalifa to Minā."» However, al-Zamakhsharī said after that: «If the report is authentic, then الضَّبْح has been borrowed for camels, just as المَشافِر (camels' lips) and الحافِر (hoof) were borrowed for humans, and the [human] lips for the colt.» Others transmitted that الضَّبْح occurs in camels, black snakes, owls, the ṣadā [owl], hares, foxes and the bow. Abū Ḥanīfa [al-Dīnawarī] quoted, describing a bow:
4618 - حَنَّانَةٌ مِنْ نَشَمٍ أو تالبِ ... تَضْبَحُ في الكَفِّ ضُباحَ الثعلبِ
(A twanging [bow] of nasham or tālib wood, which yelps in the hand like the yelping of the fox.)
In my view this is by way of metaphor. The lexicographers transmitted that the basis of الضَّبْح is in the fox, and it was borrowed for horses; and it is from ضَبَحَتْه النارُ, i.e. the fire altered its colour without going far in it; and الضَّبْح is a colour that changes slightly toward black.
The third of the views: it is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. they pant a panting, and this verb is a ḥāl of «العاديات».
The fourth: it is accusative by «العادِيات», even if what is meant by it is the sound. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «As though it were said: and by the panting ones, because panting occurs with running.» The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: «If panting is with running, then the meaning of "والعادياتِ" is not "and the panting ones", so it should not be explained by it.» I say: al-Zamakhsharī did not say that it has its meaning; he only made it accusative by it, because it is inseparably bound to it, never leaving it, so it is as if it were pronounced. His saying «As though it were said» is an explanation of the mutual inseparability, not [a claim] that it is identical with it.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {قَدْحاً}: It may be an emphasising maṣdar (verbal noun), because striking fire (الإِيراء) is from striking (القَدْح); one says: قَدَحَ فَأَوْرَى (he struck and produced fire) and قَدَح فأَصْلَدَ (he struck and failed to produce fire). It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), the meaning being: striking, i.e. knocking with their hooves what produces fire; one says: «قَدَحْتُ الحجرَ بالحجرِ», i.e. I knocked the stone against the stone. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «It is accusative by what made ضَبْحاً accusative.» He had permitted three views on its accusative: the accusative by an implied verb; the accusative by the active participle before it, because it is inseparable from it; and the accusative as a ḥāl. That fire which comes out of the hooves is called نار الحُباحِب. He said:
4619 - تَقُدُّ السُّلُوقِيَّ المُضاعَفَ نَسْجُهُ ... وتُوْقِدُ بالصُّفَّاحِ نارَ الحُباحِبِ
(They cleave the Salūqī [mail] of double weave, and kindle on the broad stones the fire of the ḥubāḥib.)

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {فالمغيرات صُبْحاً}: «صُبْحاً» is an adverbial of time, i.e. those that raid at the time of morning. One says: أغارَ يُغير إغارةً: he took his enemy by surprise for plunder, killing or capture. He said:
4620 - فلَيْتَ لي بهمُ قوماً إذا رَكِبوا ... شَنُّوا الإِغارةَ فُرْساناً ورُكْبانا
(Would that I had in their place a people who, when they ride, launch the raid, horsemen and camel-riders.)
«غار» is a minor dialectal form; and أغار and غار also [mean]: he descended into الغَوْر, which is low-lying land. People differed over what is described by these attributes, I mean «العاديات» and what follows. It was said: horses, i.e. and by the running horses, then the fire-striking ones, then the raiding ones. The parallel of the conjunction here is the conjunction in his saying:
4621 - يا لَهْفَ زيَّابةَ لِلحارِث ال ... صابحِ فالغانِمِ فالآئِبِ
(O the grief of Zayyāba for al-Ḥārith, who attacks at morning, then takes the spoil, then returns!)
Its establishment has been given at the beginning of al-Baqara. It was also said: the implied form is: and by the camels running from ʿArafa to Muzdalifa and from Muzdalifa to Minā, as preceded from the Commander of the Faithful. It is supported by the saying of Ṣafiyya bint ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib:
4622 - أمَا والعادياتِ غَداةَ جَمْعٍ ... بأَيْديها إذا سَطَع الغُبارُ
(Now, by those running on the morning of Jamʿ [Muzdalifa] with their forelegs, when the dust rises…)
It was also said: «فالموريات», i.e. the group that plots in war; the Arabs say: لأُوْرِيَنَّ لك, [meaning] I will surely plot against you.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {فَأَثَرْنَ}: He conjoined the verb onto the noun because the noun is in the sense of a verb, since it occurs as the ṣila (relative clause) of «أل». Al-Zamakhsharī said: «It is conjoined onto the verb in whose place the active participle was put», meaning originally, since the original is: واللاتي عَدَوْنَ فأَوْرَيْنَ فأغَرْنَ فَأَثَرْنَ (and by those that ran, then struck fire, then raided, then raised).
His saying: {بِهِ}: There are several views on the hāʾ. The first: it is the pronoun of the morning, i.e. they raised dust at the time of morning; and this is good, because it is mentioned explicitly. The second: it refers to the place, even though it has not been mentioned, because raising [dust] must have a place, so the context and the verb indicate it. In al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «It was also said: the pronoun is for the place of the raid (الغارة)»; this is according to that minor dialectal form; otherwise the eloquent [usage] would be to say: الإِغارة. The third: it is the pronoun of the running indicated by «والعادياتِ».
The majority read with the thāʾ undoubled, from أثار كذا, when he spreads and scatters it while raising it. Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it with doubling, and al-Zamakhsharī explained it in two ways: the first, in the sense of "they made dust appear by it", because التأثير contains the meaning of making appear; the second, that he transposed «ثَوَّرْنَ» into «وَثَّرْنَ» and changed the wāw into a hamza. End of quotation. I say: he means that the original is ثَوَّرْنَ, from ثَوَّر يُثَوِّرُ with doubling, made transitive by the doubling just as it is made transitive by the hamza in your saying أثاره; then he transposed the word by putting the middle radical, the wāw, in the place of the first radical, the thāʾ, so it became وَثَّرْنَ, whose pattern is then عَفَّلْنَ; then he changed the wāw into a hamza, so it became «أَثَّرْنَ». This is very far-fetched. And granting it, changing a fatḥa-voweled wāw into a hamza is not regular; only a few small words have come with it, such as أَحَد and أَناة. [Translator's note: the source writes the final form as «أَثَرْنَ» without doubling; the doubled form is meant.] النَّقْع is dust, and it was quoted:
4623 - يَخْرُجْنَ مِنْ مُسْتطارِ النَّقْعِ داميةً ... كأنَّ آذانَها أطرافُ أَقْلامِ
(They come out of the flying dust, bloodied, as though their ears were the tips of reed pens.)
Ibn Rawāḥa said:
4624 - عَدِمْتُ بُنَيَّتِي إنْ لَمْ تَرَوْها ... تُثير النَّقْعَ مِنْ كَنَفَيْ كَداءِ
(May I lose my little daughter if you do not see them [the horses] raising dust from both sides of Kadāʾ.)
Abū ʿUbayd said: «النَّقْع is raising the voice», and he quoted:
4625 - فمتى يَنْقَعْ صُراخٌ صادِقٌ ... يُحْلِبُوْها ذاتَ جَرْسٍ وزَجَلْ
(Whenever a true cry for help is raised, they gather it [the war] full of clamour and din.)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «It is possible that by النَّقْع shouting is meant, from his saying, peace be upon him: "ما لم يكن نَقْعٌ ولا لَقْلَقَةٌ" (as long as there is no shrieking nor wailing), and the saying of Labīd:
فمتى يَنْقَعْ صُراخٌ صادِقٌ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
i.e. they stirred up shouting in the place raided against them in the morning.» End of quotation. On this view, the bāʾ is in the sense of «في», and the pronoun refers to the place in which the raid occurs, as preceded.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {فَوَسَطْنَ}: The majority read with the sīn undoubled, i.e. they penetrated into the middle. There are several views on the hāʾ in «به». The first: it is for the morning, as preceded. The second: it is for the dust, i.e. they put the dust in the midst of the host, i.e. they made the dust [be] in the middle of the host; so the bāʾ is for transitivity (taʿdiya), while on the first [view] it is locative. The third: the bāʾ is circumstantial (for the ḥāl), i.e. they penetrated, accompanied by the dust, into a host among the hosts of the enemies. It was also said: the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted it. On these views «جَمْعاً» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The fourth: what is meant by «جَمْع» is al-Muzdalifa, which is called Jamʿ; and what is meant is that the camels penetrate into the middle of Jamʿ, which is al-Muzdalifa, as preceded from the Commander of the Faithful, may Allah be pleased with him; so what is meant by الجَمْع is a place, not a gathering of people, as in the saying of Ṣafiyya:
4626 -. . . . . . . . . . . والعادياتِ غَداةَ جَمْعٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(…and by those running on the morning of Jamʿ…)
and the saying of Bishr ibn Abī Khāzim:
4627 - فَوَسَطْنَ جَمْعَهُمُ وأَفْلَتَ حاجبٌ ... تحت العَجابةِ في الغُبارِ الأَقْتَمِ
(They penetrated into the midst of their host, and Ḥājib escaped beneath the dust-cloud, in the dark dust.)
On this view «جَمْعاً» is accusative as an adverbial of place; and on this view the pronoun in «به» is either for the time, i.e. at the time of morning, or for the dust, with the bāʾ circumstantial, i.e. accompanied by the dust. However, the accusative of a specific adverb of place is problematic, since by right [the verb] should reach it through «في». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «جَمْعاً is a ḥāl (circumstantial)», and Makkī preceded him in it. This is far-fetched, since the meaning is that the horses penetrated into the midst of the host of people.
ʿAlī, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Qatāda and Ibn Abī Laylā read it with doubling of the sīn; they are two dialectal forms with one meaning, I mean the heavy and the light [forms]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «The doubling is for transitivity, and the bāʾ is redundant for emphasis, as in His saying: {وَأُتُواْ بِهِ مُتَشَابِهاً} [al-Baqara: 25]; and it is an intensification of "وَسَطْن".» End of quotation. His saying «and it is an intensification» contradicts his earlier saying «for transitivity», because doubling for intensification does not give the verb another object; you say «ذَبَحْتُ الغنم» (I slaughtered the sheep) with the light form, then you intensify and say «ذَبَّحْتها» with the heavy form. And this [verb], according to his view, he has made transitive by itself, as shown by his making the bāʾ redundant; so it cannot be for intensification.

ukberi-tibyan:1-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالْعَادِيَاتِ ضَبْحًا (١) فَالْمُورِيَاتِ قَدْحًا (٢) فَالْمُغِيرَاتِ صُبْحًا (٣)).
The words of the Exalted (ضَبْحًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. «وَالْعَادِيَاتِ ضَابِحَةً» (by those that run, panting).
(قَدْحًا) is an emphatic maṣdar (absolute object of emphasis), because «الْمُورِي» is the one who strikes sparks («الْقَادِح»).
(صُبْحًا) is an adverbial (ẓarf).

ukberi-tibyan:4-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعًا (٤) فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعًا (٥)).
The hāʾ is the pronoun of the valley, although it has not been mentioned here. (جَمْعًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and «بِهِ» is a ḥāl as well.
It is also said that the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. «وَسَطْنَهُ» (they penetrated into its midst).

ukberi-tibyan:6-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ (٦) وَإِنَّهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ لَشَهِيدٌ (٧) وَإِنَّهُ لِحُبِّ الْخَيْرِ لَشَدِيدٌ (٨)).
(لِرَبِّهِ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «كَنُود», i.e. ungrateful for the favours of his Lord. (لِحُبِّ الْخَيْرِ) is attached to «شَدِيد», i.e. he is intense in his love of amassing wealth. It is also said that it [the lām] is in the sense of «عَلَى». [Translator's note: the printed text reads «بِتَشْدِيدٍ»; the word in the verse is «شَدِيد», and it is translated accordingly.]

ukberi-tibyan:9-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَفَلَا يَعْلَمُ إِذَا بُعْثِرَ مَا فِي الْقُبُورِ (٩) وَحُصِّلَ مَا فِي الصُّدُورِ (١٠) إِنَّ رَبَّهُمْ بِهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَخَبِيرٌ (١١)).
The words of the Exalted (إِذَا بُعْثِرَ): the governor (ʿāmil) of «إِذَا» is «يَعْلَمُ». It is also said that its governor is what the khabar (predicate) of «إِنَّ» indicates, and the meaning is: when [what is in the graves] is scattered forth, they will be recompensed. (يَوْمَئِذٍ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «خَبِير». And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-ʿĀdiyāt
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿والعادِياتِ ضَبْحًا﴾ ("by the chargers, panting"): by al-ʿādiyāt here the horses are meant. This is an oath, whose answer is ﴿إنَّ الإنْسانَ لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ﴾ [al-ʿĀdiyāt: 6] ("the human being is surely ungrateful to his Lord").
And His saying: ﴿ضَبْحًا﴾: its meaning is "by the chargers that pant a panting"; and their panting is the sound of their insides when they run.

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿فالمُورِياتِ قَدْحًا﴾ ("and the strikers of sparks"): when the horses run at night and their hooves strike the stones, sparks of fire are struck from them.

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿فالمُغِيراتِ صُبْحًا﴾ ("and the raiders at dawn"): the horses are meant. It has come in the exegesis that it was a raiding party (sariyya) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ against Kinda.

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿فَأثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعًا﴾ ("stirring up dust thereby"): ”اَلنَّقْعُ“ is dust. He said ”بِهِ“ ("thereby") although the place had not been mentioned before, but there is evidence for it in the discourse; the meaning is: "they stirred up nuqʿ in the place of their running", that is, dust.

zajjaj:5-5.t: ﴿فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعًا﴾ ("and penetrating thereby into a host"): the reading is ﴿فَوَسَطْنَ﴾, that is, they went into the middle of the place. If one said ”فَوَسَّطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعًا“ it would be permissible, except that I know of no one who read it so.

zajjaj:6-6.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ الإنْسانَ لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ﴾: its meaning is "surely ungrateful"; by that the unbeliever is meant.

zajjaj:8-8.t:
﴿وَإنَّهُ لِحُبِّ الخَيْرِ لَشَدِيدٌ﴾ ("and he is, in love of wealth, surely intense"): the meaning of ”لَشَدِيدٌ“ is "surely miserly", that is: and he, on account of love of wealth, is surely miserly. Ṭarafa said:
أرى المَوْتَ يَعْتامُ الكِرامَ ويَصْطَفِي ∗∗∗ عَقِيلَةَ مالِ الباخِلِ المُتَشَدِّدِ
(I see death choosing the generous, and selecting the choicest of the wealth of the tight-fisted miser [al-mutashaddid].)

zajjaj:9-9.t: And His saying: ﴿أفَلا يَعْلَمُ إذا بُعْثِرَ ما في القُبُورِ﴾ ("does he not know, when what is in the graves is scattered out?"): ”بُعْثِرَ“ and ”بُحْثِرَ“ have one meaning; and the meaning is: "does he not know, when the dead are resurrected?"

zajjaj:11-11.t: And His saying: ﴿إنَّ رَبَّهم بِهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَخَبِيرٌ﴾ ("their Lord, on that Day, is surely fully aware of them"): Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is aware of them on that day and on other days; but the meaning is: "Allah will requite them for their unbelief on that day", and He does not requite them except by His knowledge of their deeds. Similar to it is: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُ اللَّهُ ما في قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 63] ("those are the ones of whom Allah knows what is in their hearts"), whose meaning is: those are the ones whose requital He leaves aside. [Translator's note: so in the source, «يَتْرُكُ مُجازاتِهِمْ»; the sense intended may be that He does not leave aside requiting them.]
